questions.q: What is the most accurate definition of **Drug Abuse**?
options: Taking medications exactly as prescribed by a qualified physician
The arbitrary, excessive, or incorrect consumption of drugs without medical prescription or supervision
The process of manufacturing medicinal syrup in a laboratory
Storing drugs in a home first aid box for emergencies
questions.explain: **Drug Abuse** occurs when individuals take illicit drugs, or when they consume legal, therapeutic drugs without a doctor's prescription, in excess, or for non-medical reasons.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances

questions.q: Which of the following is considered a common **form of drug abuse** in society?
options: Receiving a vaccination at a government hospital
Taking paracetamol daily for months without seeing a doctor (Self-medication)
Eating balanced diets with sufficient vitamins
Using a plaster to cover an open wound
questions.explain: **Self-medication**—continuously diagnosing and treating oneself with drugs without professional medical advice—is a widespread and dangerous form of drug abuse.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances

questions.q: When a student habitually inhales the fumes of petroleum, correction fluid (Tipp-Ex), or rubber glue to feel 'high', they are engaging in:
options: Substance Abuse
Constructive use of time
Communal labour
Prescription drug therapy
questions.explain: Inhaling solvents and household chemicals for psychoactive effects is known as **Substance Abuse** (inhalant abuse), which heavily damages brain cells.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances

questions.q: Taking three tablets of a powerful antibiotic instead of the one tablet prescribed by the doctor, in order to 'cure the disease faster', is a form of drug abuse strictly defined as:
options: Under-dosage
Over-dosage
Placebo effect
Rehabilitation
questions.explain: Consuming more than the medically recommended amount of a drug is termed **Over-dosage**, which can severely damage the liver and kidneys.

questions.q: What is a major physiological consequence of chronic drug abuse on the **individual**?
options: Increased academic brilliance
Development of psychiatric problems (madness) and organ failure
Immunity to all infectious viral diseases
Immediate promotion at their workplace
questions.explain: On an individual level, chronic abuse of psychoactive substances destroys brain chemistry, leading to **psychiatric disorders, psychosis, and critical organ failure**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances

questions.q: How does widespread drug abuse primarily affect the **Community**?
options: It increases the number of highly skilled artisans
It fosters positive peace and harmony
It leads to a surge in crime rates, violent gang clashes, and insecurity
It results in cheaper agricultural food products
questions.explain: Within the community, drug addicts often resort to theft, armed robbery, and violence to fund their expensive addictions, causing a drastic **increase in the crime rate and insecurity**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances

questions.q: At the **national level**, what macroeconomic damage does heavy substance abuse inflict on the country?
options: It boosts national tax revenues through illegal sales
It depletes the nation's energetic youth workforce, thereby severely retarding economic productivity
It forces foreign governments to send free money to the country
It drastically increases life expectancy averages
questions.explain: Because youths (the most productive demographic) are disproportionately affected by drug abuse, the nation suffers a severe **loss of human resources and workforce**, paralyzing economic growth.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances

questions.q: Consider the consequences of drug trafficking and abuse on the **International Community** level. Which of the following best represents this?
options: Harmonious cross-border cultural festivals
Strained diplomatic relationships, international sanctions, and harsh border controls for the country's citizens
Establishment of a single global currency
Universal eradication of poverty
questions.explain: A nation known for producing and trafficking drug abusers suffers from severe diplomatic backlash, including **sanctions, strained relationships, and harsh scrutiny** by the international community.

questions.q: Mathematical logic: If $ \text{Abuse} \rightarrow \text{Addiction} $, and $ \text{Addiction} \rightarrow \text{Desperation for Funds} $, what is the ultimate societal output?
options: Communal labour and charity
Rise in theft, corruption, and communal insecurity
Better social justice
Mass graduation of university students
questions.explain: Desperation to fund an addiction frequently pushes individuals to steal from their families or engage in armed robbery, directly increasing **theft and communal insecurity**.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances

questions.q: One of the consequences of drug abuse on the **individual** is 'Social Isolation'. What does this mean?
options: The individual is celebrated by their community leaders
The individual is sent to an expensive boarding school
The individual is stigmatized, shunned by society, and abandoned by friends and family due to erratic behavior
The individual successfully campaigns for political office
questions.explain: Addicts display destructive, erratic behaviors that eventually exhaust the patience of relatives and friends, leading to **stigmatization and social isolation**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances

questions.q: A societal effect of chronic drug abuse on the nation's healthcare system is that it:
options: Provides an abundance of cheap medicine
Reduces the number of people who fall sick annually
Overburdens hospitals and psychiatric facilities, diverting national resources meant for other development
Eliminates the need for professional doctors
questions.explain: The nation spends immense sums treating addiction-related illnesses, which heavily **overburdens psychiatric facilities and drains healthcare resources**.

questions.q: Which of the following illicit substances is commonly abused by youths and is notorious for altering perception and causing severe hallucination and psychotic episodes?
options: Vitamin C supplements
Marijuana (Indian Hemp) and Cocaine
Anti-malarial drugs
Iodized salt
questions.explain: **Marijuana, cocaine, and heroin** are hard, illicit psychoactive substances strictly prohibited by law because of their severe hallucinogenic and addictive properties.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances

questions.q: Identify the incorrect statement regarding the consequences of drug abuse:
options: It ruins the academic pursuit of students due to loss of memory and expulsion
It fosters greater trust and harmony within the family as relatives support the addict
It leads to immense financial ruin for the individual
It exposes users to deadly infections like HIV/AIDS if using shared needles
questions.explain: Drug abuse does NOT foster trust. Instead, it severely **weakens family love**, creates mistrust (due to lying and stealing), and shatters the peace within the home.

questions.q: When a youth learns a coping skill described as "The ability to make rational, deeply thought-out choices after weighing the pros and cons of an action", this specific skill is:
options: Decision making skill
Resistance skill
Vocational skill
Communal skill
questions.explain: **Decision making skill** involves critical thinking; weighing the temporary pleasure of a drug against the permanent destruction of one's future, leading to the rational choice to abstain.

questions.q: Often, addicts suffer from sudden heart attacks resulting in immediate death, despite being young. This fatal reality is heavily associated with the abuse of strong central nervous system stimulants like:
options: Paracetamol
Cocaine
Water
Cough syrup in prescribed doses
questions.explain: **Cocaine** is a potent illicit stimulant that dramatically increases heart rate and blood pressure, notoriously causing sudden cardiac arrests and organ failure even in youths.

questions.q: In conclusion of the Social and Health Issues curriculum, preserving one's dignity, staying drug-free, and acquiring healthy coping skills fulfills the ultimate objective of making the student a:
options: Wealthy foreign expatriate
Good citizen, capable of contributing positively to societal development
Member of a destructive group
Mastermind of an international cartel
questions.explain: The ultimate aim of all these preventative teachings is to mold the youth into a **good citizen**, free of harmful addictions, who is willing and physically capable of contributing to the society's progress.
